evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.99: quam varia genera bēstiārum vel cicurum vel ferārum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The classical word for a kind of animal or plant: avium genera, omne genus ferārum. In modern taxonomy genus is the rank above the species (M-O s.v. species: genus), so in a scientific context use speciēs.

evidence: M-O s.v. species (plant or animal taxonomy), after Pallas (1811)
Varr. RR 3.3.3: in bīnās speciēs dīvidī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically a look, an appearance, and in logic a subdivision of a genus (Cic. de Or. 1.189, Sen. Ep. 58.7); the biological rank is modern. In Cicero’s day its genitive and dative plural were not used (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quae vērō et quam varia genera bēstiārum vel cicurum vel ferārum!
phrases.english: and what kinds of beasts, tame and wild, and how varied!

sources: Lewis & Short: genus · Lewis & Short: species
